sam: CI red on main — flaky unit TestServeRetryTiming on linux-ubuntu-22.04 runner. Fails ~3/10 runs. Logs show `context deadline exceeded` in sendLoop. Repro locally only under load. @anil @maya can you take a look?

maya: I saw something similar after the backpressure patch. Sounds like timer ordering or an edge in the retry backoff. Can you paste the failing test log and the `go test` command you used?

sam: Pasting the failing tail:```
--- FAIL: TestServeRetryTiming (0.12s)
    serve_test.go:243: unexpected error: context deadline exceeded
    rpc.go:87: sendLoop: write timeout after 50ms
FAIL
FAIL    github.com/redwood/runtime/serve   0.502s
```

sam: I run `bazel test //runtime/... --test_output=errors` locally, but only reproduces when I have a cpu-heavy loop in background.

anil: Taking a look. Two quick asks: 1) can you kick off a CI rerun with multiple attempts so we have stats? 2) if it reproduces add `--run=TestServeRetryTiming -count=10` to isolate flakiness. Also try `go test -race` once it reproduces.

sam: Kicked off rerun: https://ci.internal/redwood/job/5421 (10 runs). ci-bot should post results.

ci-bot: Rerun queued for job 5421 — 10 attempts. Will report per-attempt failures.

maya: If CI shows the same failure pattern, capture a goroutine dump and add env `TEST_PPROF=1` so we get pprof on failure. Also check runner load metrics (disk/cpu steal). This looks like IO/timer starvation more than a pure race.

anil: Local stress helper you can run: ```bash
for i in {1..200}; do go test ./runtime -run TestServeRetryTiming -count=1 || break; done
```

sam: Will run the stress loop and attach the first failing trace + CI logs back here. Thanks :thumbsup:
